newsitem.title: USA: Chicago plans $36.4 mln TIF funds for two theaters.
newsitem.headline: Chicago plans $36.4 mln TIF funds for two theaters.

text.p: Chicago planning officials received preliminary approvals for granting $36.4 million of tax-increment financing funds to developers of two downtown theater renovation projects near City Hall.

The Community Development Commission approved plans Tuesday to provide $18.8 million for a project to relocate the Goodman Theatre and $17.6 million for a renovation of the Bismarck Theater and hotel, planning spokeswoman Olga Domchenko said.

The overall $53.2 million Goodman development would bring the company to the now vacant Selwyn and Harris theater buildings and includes city demolition of a parking garage for restaurant and retail use by the developer, Chicago Theater Group Inc.
Completion of the Goodman project is anticipated in 2000.
Redevelopment of the Bismarck Hotel, Palace Theater and Metropolitan Office Building, located in a single structure, totals $74.5 million.
"We are grateful for the city's support for this important project," said Michael Moyer, managing member of Pal/Met Venture LLC, owner and developer of the Bismarck property.

Kimpton Hotel & Restaurant Group, based in San Francisco, will oversee the Bismarck renovation and operate the hotel and Fox Theatricals and Magicworks Entertainment have been contracted to operate the theater.
Bismarck renovations would be completed in fall 1998 under the plans submitted to the city.
Chicago must next advertise for alternate proposals and the plans must be submitted to the City Council for approval.
